BiblicalUsage: The word appears only in Leviticus 26, and every time it is the same charge: if you walk contrary to me, I will walk contrary to you. God does not speak this word to strangers — he speaks it to his own people, and he repeats it seven times over. Then comes the way back: if they confess their iniquity and that they have walked contrary, he remembers his covenant.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe contrary is the honest word for a heart that will not hearken, and God answers it in kind — but the same chapter that threatens sevenfold also opens the door to confession. I hold that God walks contrary to the contrary so that his people will turn, not so that they will be destroyed.
